Task packet (job-tracker, ~/Workspace/job-tracker). Each selected id (trimmed, deduplicated) must be on the board (`dataset.roles`), else reason `not on the board`; its `decisions[id].decision` must be `keep`: an `ignore` decision gives reason `decision is ignore, not keep`, a missing one `no keep decision recorded`. Return `{ selected: <count>, created: [{ id, recordId, title }], skipped: [{ id, title, matches: [recordId] }], failed: [{ id, title, reason }] }`; an error from `persistPromotion` after a create puts that role in `failed` with the error's message, and a retry then skips it instead of creating a second record.

Task packet (thermalright-display, ~/Workspace/thermalright-display). Two `FrameSender` defects in `studio/frame_sender.py` (the helper protocol: a freshly started helper first prints a `RESOLUTION` line, then answers each frame with `OK`).
1. A helper that is respawned internally (by `_replace_process`, or by the reopen path in `_current_process` after a close) is read as if its first stdout line were the frame acknowledgment, so the startup `RESOLUTION` line is misread. Drain that line from every respawned helper before `send()` treats stdout as an acknowledgment; each new helper receives the frame exactly once.

Task packet (Strata, ~/Workspace/Strata). Two Monitor metrics bugs in `serve/server.py`.
1. `live.tok_s` is `generated / (now - first_token)`, a cumulative mean whose first sample is 1/elapsed: against an engine paced at 25 tokens/s the Speed card read 27,235.7 tok/s at the first sample, then undershot for a second, and the sparkline (scaled to its 60-sample maximum) went flat for a minute. Make `tok_s` the rate over the last `RATE_WINDOW_S` (2 s); while a request is younger than `RATE_MIN_SPAN_S` (0.25 s) report the mean so far with its span floored there, so no sample can diverge (live readings stay under four times the true rate). Keep the old formula as `_tok_s_mean()`, still reported as `live.tok_s_mean` and `status.tokens_per_s_mean`. When idle, `live.state` is `idle` and `live.tok_s` is null.

Trust the engine's counters only when its DONE replaced the object captured at request start; such a request's row has `finish: "error"`, its own `output_tokens`, `decode_tok_s: null` and `engine_generated: null` (the row carries the engine's own token count as `engine_generated` when there is one).
